title: Letters hide the truth from our eyes: English homophones have meaningfully different phonetic realizations
abstract: arXiv:2608.26749v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The distribution of spoken word duration of English homophones is known to co-vary with frequency of use. This study investigates whether other aspects of the phonetic realization of homophones also differ. A series of quantitative investigations of 14,000 homophone tokens in American television news broadcasts revealed that the tokens of homophone pairs such as \textit{weight} and \textit{wait} have different phonetic realizations, and that these can be predicted from their meanings in utterance context. These systematic differences remain even when taking duration-related variation into account. Time-normalized spectrograms emerged as an excellent tool for probing the fine details of phonetic realization, and obviate the need for phonetic transcriptions, which inevitably hide the phonetic truth from our eyes.

translated_title: 字母掩盖了我们眼中的真相：英语同音词在语音实现上存在有意义的差异
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26749v1 公告类型：新 摘要：已知英语同音词的口语词长分布与使用频率共变。本研究探讨同音词在语音实现的其他方面是否也存在差异。通过对美国电视新闻广播中14,000个同音词标记进行一系列定量研究，发现诸如“weight”和“wait”等同音词对的标记具有不同的语音实现，且这些差异可根据其在话语语境中的含义进行预测。即使在考虑与时长相关的变异后，这些系统性差异仍然存在。时间归一化频谱图成为探测语音实现细节的绝佳工具，并消除了对语音转录的需求，因为转录不可避免地会掩盖我们眼中的语音真相。
tldr: 本研究通过分析大量英语同音词，发现其语音实现差异与语境含义相关，并采用时间归一化频谱图揭示了传统转录所掩盖的语音细节。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that English homophones exhibit meaning-related phonetic differences, uncovered via time-normalized spectrograms, which surpass traditional transcription limitations.
